short: Fought a civil war to hold the union together and ended slavery in doing it.
full:
Seven states had already left the union when Lincoln was inaugurated in March 1861; four more followed the firing on Fort Sumter in April. He suspended habeas corpus, blockaded the southern coast, and raised armies far beyond anything the peacetime republic had contemplated, defending each step as a war power belonging to the presidency.

The Emancipation Proclamation, effective 1 January 1863, turned a war for the union into a war against slavery and opened the army to black soldiers, some 180,000 of whom served. Re-elected in November 1864 after Sherman took Atlanta, Lincoln pressed the Thirteenth Amendment through the House in January 1865. Lee surrendered at Appomattox on 9 April. Five days later John Wilkes Booth shot him at Ford's Theatre; he died the following morning, 15 April, the first American president to be assassinated.
